images.caption: Figure 1:NexSight overview.(1)Verifiable task construction (SightForge):dense raw-video evidence, answer-hidden verification, and counterexample checks establish reliable tasks. (2)Multiscale active evaluation (SightLine and SightLoop):a 310-task benchmark and interactive harness assess temporal exploration, local inspection, and evidence integration. (3)Agentic post-training (Sight-35B):QA supervision and separately collected solver trajectories improve interactive accuracy by 20.97 percentage points over Base and support Direct-64 transfer to Video-MME Long and LVBench (123-question subset).

Figure 2:Six core capabilities and task distribution of SightLine.The benchmark covers unlocalized fact retrieval without timestamp cues, ordering of separated events, counting across temporal windows without duplication, identity tracking across occlusions and shot changes, state/attribute change recognition, and temporal boundary localization. The donut chart shows the task count and percentage for each capability (310 tasks in total).

Figure 3:SightForge: verification before acceptance.The verifier reconstructs an answer from the question and reacquired evidence, without seeing the draft answer or generation reasoning. Comparison, independent review, and counterexample checks gate acceptance; unresolved candidates return for additional evidence or revision, or are rejected. Solver trajectories are collected separately on training tasks.

Figure 4:Overall model performance on SightLine.Accuracy over 310 tasks across fixed-input Direct and interactive SightLoop configurations (Ledger On/Off). Each model has two overlaid bars: Direct-64/128 and Ledger On/Off. The top and rounded internal boundary mark scores, not their sum. Reference models are ordered by their highest score, followed by Sight-35B. Model sources: GPT-5.6 Sol[20], DeepSeek V4 Flash Vision[6], Nex-N2.5-Mini[19], Qwen3.5-397B-A17B[24], and Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-Base[23].

Figure 7:SightLoop (Ledger On) capability accuracy (%) on the 310-task SightLine benchmark; row labels give task counts. Sight-35B gains most over Base in cross-window count and state change under combined post-training, complementing the temporal-localization diagnostic in Sec.6.2.

Figure A1:SightLine benchmark overview and distributions.The benchmark contains 310 tasks from 108 long videos across six fine-grained capabilities. The figure summarizes benchmark statistics, task proportions by capability and content domain, and the distribution of reference evidence artifacts per task.

images.caption: Figure A3:SightLoop multiscale active observation.Given a question and video overview, the video agent selects temporal windows, invokes an image agent for local inspection, integrates returned evidence, and revisits observations as needed. The image agent uses the same evaluated VLM. Optional Ledger memory retains observations across turns; calls, frames, pixels, and tokens are governed by explicit budgets, while actions, observations, and timestamps are logged.

Figure A5:Qualitative diagnosis of agentic long-video problem solving (GPT-5.6 Sol).Left:SightLoop timeline ticks indicate returned overview frames, and blue bars show the union of local observation windows. Neither GT evidence group (at∼\sim81 s and 172 s) is intersected by the explored windows, whereas supplying GT frames recovers the correct answer.Right:Complete GT evidence is supplied, yet the model response omits the required posture transition.

Figure A6:Qualitative comparison of fixed vs. active evidence acquisition (GPT-5.6 Sol).Under an identical observation budget, Fixed-Window sampling misses both annotated evidence points and answers incorrectly. Active selection redirects subsequent windows toward the end-card region after observing the cooldown segment, capturing the target promotional URL (BODiPreviews.com) and answering correctly (Rihit=1/2R_{i}^{\mathrm{hit}}=1/2).
